title: Tolerate ENOENT in overlay safety check's concurrent readdir+stat walk
context: safeOverlayTree and overlayAttributeSourcesAreSafe both scan directories and stat files, but have a TOCTOU race: a concurrent sibling clone's atomic temp-file+rename can delete an entry between readdir listing it and lstat/realpath checking it. A prior fix addressed the second check; this one fixes the same vulnerability in the first check. CI failures reproduced the exact refusal on windows-latest. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Wrap lstat+realpath in try-catch, skip ENOENT errors (benign concurrent deletion) but throw all other errors (real permissions/IO problems). Distinguish between concurrent-churn and actual overlay-safety failures.
consequences: Overlay safety check is resilient to benign concurrent atomic writes in peer clones.
No false-positive refusals from in-flight temp-file operations.
Real permission and I/O errors still fail loudly (not masked by ENOENT tolerance).
alternatives_rejected: Catch all readdir-to-stat errors silently (hides real problems).
Retry lstat/realpath (still vulnerable to the same race on retry).
Add locking around the walk (incompatible with atomic temp-file+rename pattern already in use elsewhere).
Leave the first walk unfixed (asymmetric vulnerability, CI failures continue).
